These definitions concern regulatory requirements applicable to registered investment companies and business development companies (collectively, \"funds\") as well as investment advisers. The definitions are used specifically for purposes of the Regulatory Flexibility Act (the \"RFA\"), which requires the Commission to consider the impact of its regulations on small entities. The amendments are designed to modernize the definitions, by increasing certain asset-based thresholds, including a mechanism for periodic future inflation adjustments, and eliminating the threshold based on total assets for advisers. In connection with these amendments, the Commission is making conforming amendments to Form ADV as well as the rule that allows certain small SEC-registered advisers to apply for a continuing hardship exemption from making Advisers Act filings electronically.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22739","title":"Medicare Program: Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment Systems; and Quality Reporting Programs; including the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Program; Request for Information on Strengthening the Standardization and Comparability of Hospital Price Transparency (HPT) Data; Prior Authorization; Accrediting Organization (AO) Deeming for Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA); and Notices of Closure of Teaching Hospitals and Opportunities To Apply for Available Slots","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22739/medicare-program-hospital-outpatient-prospective-payment-and-ambulatory-surgical-center-payment","summary":"This final rule with comment period revises the Medicare Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and the Medicare Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) payment system for calendar year 2027 based on our continuing experience with these systems. We also describe the changes to the amounts and factors used to determine the payment rates for Medicare services paid under the OPPS and those paid under the ASC payment systems. In addition, this final rule with comment period updates and refines the requirements for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program. There are no changes to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program. We finalized the expansion of the prior authorization requirement to include additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services. We also finalized implementation of certain provisions of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, for off-campus outpatient departments of a provider. In addition, this final rule with comment period announces notices of closure of teaching hospitals and opportunities to apply for available slots. Additionally, we finalized the policy that hospital accrediting organizations (AOs) with deeming authority may assess compliance with certain Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during accreditation and reaccreditation surveys.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22735","title":"Heightened Requirements for Foreign Importers of Record","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22735/heightened-requirements-for-foreign-importers-of-record","summary":"This document amends the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) regulations, consistent with Section 2 of Executive Order 14411, \"Strengthening Customs Enforcement,\" by establishing new requirements for foreign importers of record (IORs) when making entry, and corresponding responsibilities for licensed customs brokers with regard to their clients. The new regulations also set forth consequences for foreign IORs and customs brokers who fail to comply with the new requirements.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22734","title":"Drawbridge Operation Regulation; Harlem River, Between the Boroughs of Manhattan and the Bronx, New York City, New York","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22734/drawbridge-operation-regulation-harlem-river-between-the-boroughs-of-manhattan-and-the-bronx-new","summary":"The Coast Guard proposes to temporarily modify the operating regulation that governs the Macombs Dam Bridge across the Harlem River, mile 3.2, between the Boroughs of Manhattan and the Bronx, New York City, New York. The bridge owner, New York City Department of Transportation (NYCDOT), submitted a request on August 31, 2026, to allow the bridge to remain in the closed position from February 1, 2027, through November 30, 2027, and facilitate rehabilitation of the bridge structure. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22728","title":"Document Image System (DIS) Pilot for Used Self-Propelled Vehicles Export Document Submission: Renewal of Test","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22728/document-image-system-dis-pilot-for-used-self-propelled-vehicles-export-document-submission-renewal","summary":"This notice announces that U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is renewing the Document Image System (DIS) Pilot for Used Self- Propelled Vehicles (USPV) Export Document Submission (DIS USPV Test) for an additional two years. This voluntary pilot evaluates the feasibility of using the DIS to allow participants to submit the required vehicle ownership documentation for USPVs to CBP. 3-CMC) in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). Although 3-chloromethcathinone is not specifically listed in schedule I of the CSA with its own unique drug code, it is a schedule I controlled substances in the United States because it is a positional isomer of 4-chloromethcathinone, which is a schedule I hallucinogen. Therefore, DEA is simply amending the schedule I hallucinogenic substances list in its regulations to separately include 3- chloromethcathinone.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22716","title":"Change in Bank Control Notices; Acquisitions of Shares of a Bank or Bank Holding Company","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22716/change-in-bank-control-notices-acquisitions-of-shares-of-a-bank-or-bank-holding-company","summary":"","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22714","title":"Blue Earth County, Minnesota; Notice of Reasonable Period of Time for Water Quality Certification Application","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22714/blue-earth-county-minnesota-notice-of-reasonable-period-of-time-for-water-quality-certification","summary":"","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22713","title":"Meeting of the U.S. Naval Academy Board of Visitors","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22713/meeting-of-the-us-naval-academy-board-of-visitors","summary":"The DoD is publishing this notice to announce that the following Federal Advisory Committee meeting of the U.S. Naval Academy Board of Visitors, hereafter \"Board,\" will take place.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"}]}
